title: Source follower: gain with body effect and real bias source

sections.heading: The idea
sections.body_md:
The **source follower** (common drain) drives the gate and takes the output at the source; the drain sits at the supply. The source tracks the gate one \(V_{GS}\) below it, so the stage is a buffer. It has a gain just under 1, the gate's infinite input resistance, and a low output resistance. That makes it the stage of choice for driving small loads that would crush a CS stage's gain.

The gain falls short of 1 for two reasons, and this skill owns both. First, everything hanging on the source node divides the output: the device's own \(r_o\), the bias source's output resistance \(r_{oc}\), and any load. Second, with the body grounded the source signal also appears as \(v_{bs} = -v_{out}\). The body source \(g_{mb}v_{bs}\) then fights the output, so even with an ideal load the gain is \(g_m/(g_m + g_{mb})\). The output resistance is \(1/(g_m + g_{mb})\) in parallel with the resistances at the source.

sections.heading: Key equations
sections.body_md:
\[ A_v = \frac{g_m}{g_m + g_{mb} + 1/r_o + 1/r_{oc} + 1/R_L} \]
\[ R_{out} = \frac1{g_m + g_{mb}}\parallel r_o\parallel r_{oc}, \qquad V_{out} = V_{in} - V_{GS} \ (\text{DC}) \]

sections.heading: Worked example
sections.body_md: A follower with \(g_m = 3\ \mathrm{mS}\) and \(g_{mb} = 0.6\ \mathrm{mS}\) is biased by a source with \(r_{oc} = 50\ \mathrm{k\Omega}\) (\(r_o\) large). Its gain is \(3/(3 + 0.6 + 0.02) = 0.83\), and its output resistance is about 276 Ω. Driving a 500 Ω load drops the gain to \(3/5.62 = 0.53\).

sections.heading: Common pitfalls
sections.body_md:
- Ignoring \(g_{mb}\) when the body is grounded; it often costs 10 to 20% of the gain.
- Treating the bias source as ideal; its \(r_{oc}\) loads the output.
- Forgetting the DC level shift when planning headroom.

sections.heading: Where this leads
sections.body_md: Followers buffer high-impedance stages, shift DC levels between stages, and, through bootstrapping of \(C_{gs}\), give wide bandwidth.
